body:
This seems to be intentional, the docs already state: _"This can also be used as **additional decoration between the two buttons**."_
Which implies it's drawn with the up/down buttons.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/49cc57a75dfd262bd49698910595becf3aae597b/doc/classes/SpinBox.xml#L133-L135

The docs could be made clearer. E.g. it could be mentioned that `updown` texture is drawn behind `up`/`down` textures, and that it's drawn on top of `up_background`/`down_background` StyleBoxes.

For reference they're being drawn here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/49cc57a75dfd262bd49698910595becf3aae597b/scene/gui/spin_box.cpp#L435-L442

---

The up/down customization was added in #89265.
cc @davthedev
cc @KoBeWi (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89265#issuecomment-1984758509)


---

As a workaround you could assign transparent/invalid texture as relevant up/down icons, e.g. an AtlasTexture with no `atlas` assigned:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9907dd43-a23c-481b-9be1-396ee9824256)

The potential deprecation of `updown` wasn't properly addressed. I still think it should be deprecated; if we want a background property, it should be a separate one with a better name 🙃

The current behavior broke compatibility with projects that use custom `updown` icon. Maybe we could automatically hide the separate arrows if a non-empty `updown` icon is provided.
